pr_title: Only set base in Sprite3D when needed
pr_body:
Fixes: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/48118

Instead of resetting the base mesh on every update, we just reset the base mesh when a texture is added or removed. 

The issue came from the way lights are linked to meshes in the VisualServer. The dependency between the light and the mesh was unlinked as a result of resetting the base, so the mesh wasn't being updated to remove the light from it's list of lights.

issue_context.title: Error "getornull: Condition !id_map.has(p_rid.get_data())" showing up when changing property of a sprite 3D with a deleted light source
issue_context.body:
The error message :

```
getornull: Condition "!id_map.has(p_rid.get_data())" is true. Returned: __null
   At: ./core/rid.h:160 @ getornull()
```

Is displayed everytime you change a property of a sprite3D (Like the current frame or the opacity) that has been touched by a light source that no longer exist until another light source touch it.
Even if the sprite is out of range of the light source when it get removed, the moment the light stop existing the error will begin showing up.
Only spotlights or omnilights trigger the problem.

Tested on 3.3-stable as well as on a 3.2.4RC1 that was laying around.

Here is a small project displaying the issue :

[test_light.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/6361615/test_light.zip)
comments: Can you reproduce this after disabling [BVH](https://godotengine.org/article/godot-3-3-has-arrived#dynamic-bvh) in the Project Settings?
Yes, disabling BVH does not solve the issue.

> Tested on the lastest stable release as well as on a 3.2.4RC1 that was laying around.

Please clarify what "latest stable release" means, in a few weeks time this will be different from what you mean today and contributors shouldn't have to look up the chronology of releases to infer this information. (That's why the issue template you deleted asks for this explicitly.)

Tested a few releases, this appears to be a regression in 3.2.3-stable (compared to 3.2.2-stable which does not produce the error). Happens as early as 3.2.3-beta1.

Probably related to #39867.

Error is coming from this line:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/48d7eff3e36b4e0b9e15266d2a84d32c1e43db93/drivers/gles3/rasterizer_scene_gles3.cpp#L1756

Still can't figure out why Sprite3D is triggering the error.

review_comments: Probably a silly question, but what happens if the mesh is valid but not the texture, does it get into a loop of `set_base(mesh)` then `set_base(RID())`? If so is this problematic? I'm not really familiar with the `set_base` stuff. :blush:
The mesh should always be valid! It is created in the beginning and used throughout. There is no way to set or remove a mesh. So no risk of getting into a loop.
I guess we could add ``&& texture.is_valid()`` to the first conditional so that it only resets the base when a new texture is set.
